blocks.content: The Vice President of India is the second highest constitutional office in the country. He or she acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and performs the duties of the President when the office of the President falls vacant. The provisions related to the Vice President are given in Articles 63–71 of the Constitution of India.
1. Constitutional Articles Related to Vice President

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 63 provides for the Vice President of India, who occupies the second-highest constitutional office in the country.
The Vice President is elected by an electoral college comprising all members (both elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament.
Qualifications require being an Indian citizen, at least 35 years old, and qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
Serves as the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha and acts as President during vacancies in the President's office for a maximum period of 6 months.
Removal requires a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of Rajya Sabha (effective majority) and agreed to by Lok Sabha (simple majority).

cells: Vice President to be ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha
Vice President acts as President in absence of President
Discharge of President's functions in other contingencies

blocks.content: 2. Election of the Vice President
• The Vice President is elected indirectly.
• The Electoral College consists of members of both Houses of Parliament.
• Both elected and nominated members of Parliament participate in the election.
• The election uses proportional representation with single transferable vote.
3. Qualifications for Vice President
• Must be a citizen of India.
• Must be at least 35 years of age.
• Must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
Chapter 20: Vice President of India
• Must not hold any office of profit.
4. Term of Office
• The Vice President holds office for a term of five years.
• He or she can be re-elected.
• The Vice President continues in office until a successor assumes office.
5. Powers and Functions
As Chairman of Rajya Sabha

rows: Elected members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
All members (Elected and Nominated) of Parliament only
Must be qualified for election to Lok Sabha
Must be qualified for election to Rajya Sabha
Can be initiated in either House of Parliament
Can be initiated ONLY in the Rajya Sabha

blocks.content: • Presides over the meetings of Rajya Sabha.
• Maintains discipline and order in the House.
• Decides points of order.
As Acting President
• Acts as President when the office of President becomes vacant.
• Performs presidential duties during absence or illness of the President.
6. Removal of Vice President
• The Vice President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha.
• The resolution must be approved by a majority of members of Rajya Sabha.

items: Nominated members of Parliament participate in the Vice President's election, whereas they do NOT participate in the President's election.
State Legislative Assemblies (MLAs) have NO role in the election or removal of the Vice President.
A resolution for the removal of the Vice President can ONLY be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, not in the Lok Sabha.

blocks.content: • The Lok Sabha must agree to the resolution.
EXAM Important Facts
• Vice President is ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
• Term of office is five years.
• First Vice President of India – Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.
• Election involves members of both Houses of Parliament.
